key_insight: A weakly supervised deep learning model (MIMIC) can triage early-stage mycosis fungoides on whole-slide histology, helping separate it from benign inflammatory dermatoses with high sensitivity.
clinical_relevance: As a screening aid at first-slide review, the model may reduce unnecessary ancillary testing and speed up workup while keeping missed MF cases very low.
method: Weakly supervised attention-based multiple-instance learning on 3,339 WSIs from two Dutch centers.
External validation on 371 WSIs from four independent European centers.
Blinded reader study versus 11 pathologists, then retraining and prospective-style testing in a held-out consecutive cohort.
evidence_signal: The updated model reached AUROC 0.87 in the held-out cohort, with 97.8% sensitivity and 50.2% specificity at a prespecified 0.04 threshold, reducing ancillary workups by 39.9 per 100 screening cases.
watch_item: Performance depends on validation setting and threshold calibration, so real-world deployment needs local review, spectrum-aware calibration, and monitoring for center-specific drift.
paper_title: Histological triage of early-stage mycosis fungoides using a weakly supervised deep learning-based model: a multicentre, external validation, and clinical utility study
